list.#group_ll_bars: How well your current model fits the given data. You want to maximize only the gray part, which subtracts the regularization penalty shown in red in order to discourage overfitting.
list.#cheat_button: Reveal the weights of the true distribution, and its regularized log-likelihood.
list.#group_true_ll_bars: How well the true generating model fits the given data.
list.#new_challenge: Sample a new training dataset from a new probability distribution. From the new gray counts, you can then try to estimate the secret weights that define the new distribution.
list.#new_counts: Sample a new training dataset from the same probability distribution. Small datasets can differ dramatically, leading you to different estimates of the weights. Regularization tries to reduce this variance.
list.#regularization_header: Penalize your LL score as the weights move away from 0.  This subtracts some of the gray LL bar (turning it red).
list.#ell1_regularization_span: Penalize your LL score in proportion to the weights' distance from 0. If C is large, this may make 0 the best choice for many weights.
list.#ell2_regularization_span: Penalize your LL score in proportion to the weights' squared distance from 0. Compared to ℓ1, the ℓ2 option penalizes small weights less and large weights more.
list.#regularization_constant: The strength of the regularizer. By doubling C, you double the penalty for large weights.
list.#show_gradient_span: Shows which direction you should nudge each weight, and how much that will help the gray LL bar.
list.#gradient_step: How strongly the "Step" button nudges the weights.
list.#step_button: Nudge all the weights (sliders) at once, in the direction of the gradient.  A gentle enough nudge will lengthen the gray LL bar (unless it has already reached its maximum).
list.#solve_button: Take enough steps to maximize the length of the gray LL bar. This finds the best feature weights (sliders) given the observed counts (gray outlines).
list..num_tokens_context_div: The total number of observations in this context.  (Changing it will rescale all the gray counts.)
list.#zero_weights_button: Reset all weights to zero.  Then nothing distinguishes the outcomes in each context: they all get the same probability.
list.#trellis_select_span: Choose which input to show the trellis for.
list.#trellis_show_best_span: Mark the single most probable path (found by the Viterbi algorithm).
list.#trellis_show_ab_span: Label each state with α (total weight of all paths from the first state to this one) and β (total weight of all paths from this state to the last one).
list.#trellis_show_edge_probs_span: Label each edge with the probability that the path uses it, given the input.
list.#trellis_disaggregate: Split the paths through this trellis into groups, and draw each group separately.  An edge's probability in the full trellis is the total over the groups.
list.#trellis_dataset: Choose which taggings were observed, and how many times.  Then click "Solve" to retrain.
list.#trellis_show_tags_span: Show the most probable tags under each word, colored by comparing them with the training data.
